newsitem.title: USA: Man charged with decapitating wife and son.
newsitem.headline: Man charged with decapitating wife and son.

text.p: A subway cleaner was arraigned Tuesday on charges of decapitating his wife and their son and killing the boy's half-brother, authorities said.
Richard Timmons, 33, who was charged with first- and second-degree murder, did not enter a plea at the arraignment.
He was being held without bail, Queens District Attorney's office spokeswoman Mary de Bourbon said.

Timmons previously pleaded guilty to assaulting his wife Annita Stewart Timmons, a 33-year-old hospital clerk. He was freed from jail 10 days before the brutal killings that left even veteran police investigators shaken.

Despite the previous attack, Annita Timmons admitted him to her apartment at a public housing project, police said. She had a limited court order of protection that still allowed her husband to have contact with her.

Police alleged Timmons assaulted his wife and family late on Sunday, cut off his wife's head and that of his son Aaron, 7, and fatally stabbed Aaron's half-brother, Sharrone, 13. He then slashed his own wrists.
Aaron was heard pleading for mercy when he called the 911 emergency number during the attack. "Daddy, stop it!" he shouted. Police recovered a kitchen knife and hatchet from the apartment.

De Bourbon said Timmons pleaded guilty to assault and other charges stemming from 1996 attacks on his wife. He was released after nine months in jail. Prosecutors objected to his release and argued for a stronger order of protection.
"We felt she should have had an order that would have kept him from going anywhere near her," she said.
